extracted.intended_audience: small business owners, marketers, and PR professionals who write and distribute press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on common mistakes to avoid when drafting and distributing press releases so they are newsworthy and likely to be picked up by journalists. Emphasizes timing, writing, formatting, distribution strategy, and assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of Newsworthy Angle
rubrics_metrics.description: Without a newsworthy angle, journalists are unlikely to cover your story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test: Would a journalist write about this without your release?

rubrics_metrics.name: Poor Timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases distributed too late lose relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send before, not after, the news event happens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bad Writing Quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Poor prose and mechanical mistakes undermine credibility and reduce pickup likelihood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
- Grammatical errors
- Stiff or unnatural writing
- Wrong style usage
- Excessively long drafts
- Even one typo damages credibility

rubrics_metrics.name: Weak Headlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic headlines fail to grab attention and convey the story's value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid generic headlines like "Company X Announces New Product"; headlines should be: specific, clear, and tied to real benefits or impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overly Promotional Tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Marketing language makes a release read like an ad rather than news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid phrases such as "Leading provider of innovative solutions," "We're thrilled to announce," marketing-speak, and unsupported superlatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry Jargon
rubrics_metrics.description: Excessive technical terms create barriers between the story and the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use accessible language; every technical term builds barriers between story and audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poor Formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Dense, unscannable formatting reduces readability and journalist engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
- Long paragraphs
- Missing subheads
- Dense blocks of text
- No white space

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing Visuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Text-only releases limit engagement and pickup potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wrong Distribution Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Sending releases to the wrong people or at the wrong times reduces effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
- Don't blast every contact
- Don't send to irrelevant beats
- Don't send during breaking news, weekends, off-hours

rubrics_metrics.name: Unclear Call to Action
rubrics_metrics.description: Vague endings or missing contact paths hinder follow-up and conversion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't end with "Learn more soon" or omit contact info; provide a clear next step and contact details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing Quote
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotes humanize the release and provide credibility; omitting them weakens the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include 1-2 quotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burying the Lead
rubrics_metrics.description: Hiding the main news makes journalists hunt for the story and reduces pickup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't make journalists hunt for the news—put the key info up front.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using Wrong Person
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotes or spokespeople without authority or relevance undermine credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quote should be from someone with authority and relevance to the announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Embargo Discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Misusing embargoes damages trust with journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Misusing embargoes burns bridges with journalists—respect agreed embargoes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wrong Audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Reaching the wrong readers or outlets wastes effort and reduces pickup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor the release to the specific reader/outlet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Too Many Topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Packing multiple news items into one release confuses the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One press release = one news event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forgotten Boilerplate
rubrics_metrics.description: Omitting the company boilerplate leaves journalists without background context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include the "About [Company]" boilerplate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing Contact
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of clear contact details prevents journalists from following up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make it easy to follow up—include name, email, phone, and time zone.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Multimedia Assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of multimedia reduces engagement and likelihood of coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include photos, videos, infographics to increase pickup probability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word Count Issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Wrong length can either lack substance or be too long for busy readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
- Too short (no substance)
- Too long (over 800 words rare)
- Sweet spot: 300-500 words for news, 500-800 for features

rubrics_metrics.name: Sending Without Follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to follow up reduces chances of coverage, but over-following annoys journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow up, but not too many times—1-2 follow-ups maximum.
